analyst_view.overall: Real Sociedad II (Sanse) drew 0-0 at Sabadell on Monday, a result that lifted Jon Ansotegi's side out of the relegation zone; they hit the bar and had a goal ruled out for offside. Sporting's attack is badly depleted: Juan Otero is suspended after his red card against Valladolid, and two reports agree Nicolás Larcamón is also without Alejo Sarco (muscle problem), Antonio Casas, Konrad de la Fuente, César Gelabert, Pablo García and Manu Rodríguez. Sarco and Casas share the club's scoring lead with Guille Rosas on three goals; Andrés Ferrari is back after eight months out but not fully fit. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I have changed my lean from higher to lower: Sporting are without Otero, Sarco and Casas, three of their main forwards, and have scored only 14 in 13 games. Sanse's last game was a 0-0 in which they missed clear chances.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I stay there. Sporting keep the ball (5,966 passes in 13 games by LaLiga's count) and Sanse like to attack down the right through Díaz, their top assister with five, so corners should come at both ends.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. I still lean higher: LaLiga has Sanse on 231 fouls committed in 13 games, the most of any team in this round's previews I checked, and both sides have 37 yellows and two reds. Sanse took three more yellows at Sabadell on Monday.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. I have moved from same to lower: Sporting's weakened forward line makes their volume less likely, and LaLiga counts both teams under ten shots a game this season (128 for Sanse, 122 for Sporting). Ferrari may play some minutes, but he is short of fitness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Sporting's top scorers are missing, and Sanse put few efforts on target in their 0-0 at Sabadell. Gorosabel and Astiazaran, Sanse's top scorers, have three goals each.
